title: Image says it 100%
author: harry_potter_goat
selftext:
I'm a ex-Googler, building a GitHub only for AI game devs. hear me out...

please tell me your biggest PAIN while collab with other vibe coders, then I'll solve it.

For me, it’s Version Control + Handoff. When someone gives me their version, I don’t wanna open the code and play detective lol. I want AI to just show me what changed visually.

Like:

* before/after gameplay screenshots
* what changed in the player flow

What’s your biggest PAIN when collab with your AI game dev team?

comments.author: ao3_nuts
comments.body: Literally this. I just wanna see what actually changed in the game lol

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: Comments leaking into the frontend. A lot of that can be prevented by being very specific in the briefing, but GenAI coding agents for me tend to overload the UI with instructions and information that should really be comments or just "in the manual" and read like it's trying to justify its decisions *to the user*.

replies.author: harry_potter_goat
replies.body:
Yep, totally get this. The “AI explaining itself inside the actual UI” thing is weirdly common, and it’s annoying because it looks fine at first glance until you realize the product is full of dev-note energy.

When that happens for you, is the bigger pain cleaning up the UI copy itself, or later figuring out which parts were intentional vs AI clutter?

replies.author: harry_potter_goat
replies.body: 100% yes. I’ve been thinking about this a lot too. Could you DM me the problems you’ve been running into?

replies.author: harry_potter_goat
replies.body:
Yeah, models and textures seem like a huge one.

Is the main pain getting them to look consistent across the game, or more about the time it takes to generate/edit/import them into the actual build?

comments.author: RoryOS
comments.body:
The biggest issue I have had of late is half the ai, half myself. My character controller is bumping the roof when trying to jump out from under a low ceiling which kills the jump. I've to circle back on fixing it because none of my attempts managed and I got a bunch of extra controls and timers cluttering up the code until I stripped them out when I gave up for the time being. 

The issue was not clarifying the ask I think, which I'm now building into my change implementation process to ensure my descriptions don't fail me. 

Change control is a factor though because an early build did fix it and I didn't notice it breaking again so that's lost

replies.author: harry_potter_goat
replies.body:
This makes a lot of sense. The worst part is when one version actually fixed the issue, but then it quietly breaks again and you only realize later.

For change control, what would’ve helped most there: being able to compare playable builds, see a visual before/after of the jump behavior, or just a clearer history of what each AI/code change was supposed to do?

replies.author: RoryOS
replies.body:
To be honest with my current scenario I'm ignoring the problem to come back to it. I spent too much time trying to fix it and it's an edge case I can avoid in my level layouts.

I will revisit it but I want to get other missing features built in first

comments.author: Repulsive-Way3283
comments.body: Logic and connection between what stays in backend and what manifests in the screen

replies.author: harry_potter_goat
replies.body: YES 100%. This is exactly the kind of problem I keep thinking about. Could you DM me what you’ve been running into? I’d love to understand it better.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body: This isn't even an joke, my biggest pain is Asset developers. Too many people think making assets is an good way to make money, so the stores are flooded with code assets, making the upload processes for art assets people actually do buy, slower.
